metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in early January to assess progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that having the army rule is good.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Vietnam agree that having the army rule is good.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 4th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey, Kim. Have you thought about holding the joint meeting on January 4th? It seems like a good date to assess our progress. 

Also, I wanted to ask... what’s your take on having army rule in countries? I personally think it's not a good system.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: January 4th... sounds reasonable. We can assess progress then. But, uh, about the army rule... in Vietnam, many people believe it brings stability and order. It’s important for our country's strength. I think it can be a good system. What do you think about that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I understand that some might see it as a way to maintain stability, but I still believe that it's not beneficial in the long run. A system without enough freedom usually struggles to progress. I think people should have a say in how they are governed. 

By the way, are there any other dates you’re considering for the meeting, or is January 4th set?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I don’t really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out in their own ways. At the end of the day, it’s all the same—we all want progress. But about the meeting, January 4th sounds good, right? I think it’s important to set a date and stick to it. Are there any other dates you think we should consider?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: I see your point about wanting progress, but I still think that freedom is crucial for real development. As for the meeting, January 4th is fine with me. I don’t have any other dates in mind, so let’s stick to that.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: Great! January 4th it is then. I think we’ll have a productive discussion. And just to revisit the army rule topic... I believe it plays a big role in maintaining order. Stability is really vital for a country’s growth. Do you think that perspective could change over time?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I get that stability is important, but I really believe that true growth comes from allowing people to express themselves and participate in governance. I doubt my perspective will change on that. It’s just a core belief of mine. 

But let's focus on the meeting! January 4th is confirmed, right?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: Yes, January 4th is confirmed. I appreciate your commitment to the date. And about the governance thing... I just think that in some cases, people might not understand what’s best for them. Stability through army rule has its advantages. But for now, we’ve set the meeting, which is good. Looking forward to it!
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I understand your perspective, but I still believe that everyone deserves a voice in their governance. I think the potential for innovation and progress is much greater when people are free to express their ideas. 

But yes, let’s focus on the positive. January 4th is a step in the right direction for our project. Looking forward to it too!
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: Absolutely, January 4th is a good step. I agree it’s important to focus on our project. However, I still believe that having the army rule can create a foundation that allows for that innovation and progress to happen more securely. But let’s keep our attention on the meeting and making it successful. See you there!
turns.label: Acceptance
